title: RightsEvent — domain-neutral EP-typed rights event (canonical dict form)
$comment: Extracted from reference-implementation/rights_events/schema.py:129-197 (RightsEvent, validated in __post_init__) and its to_dict() form (schema.py:201-219). Domain-agnostic by contract: 'Field names must make sense for a parcel as well as a song' (contracts/completed/C1-event-layer.md:103-105). Proven on two domains with this schema byte-identical between them (C2-second-domain.md:276-278). This JSON Schema describes the dict that to_dict() produces / from_dict() accepts strictly (schema.py:222-272: exact key set, no additions).

kind.$comment: schema.py:63 (_EVENT_KIND); from_dict rejects any other kind (schema.py:240-243).

event_id.$comment: Examples from the proven domains: split-sheet 'evt:song-x:reg-a' style ids emitted by adapters/pro_conflict.py; parcels deed-document ids emitted by adapters/cook_parcels.py:218 (parse_deeds).

event_type.$comment: Closed set of six (schema.py:45-52; declared closed at C1-event-layer.md:27-28). Second domain needed no seventh type: deed=grant, roll/tax-sale=chain_assertion, redemption=revocation, conflicts=dispute (C2-second-domain.md:276-278).

subject_ids.$comment: A subject is any identifiable thing a claim can be about (schema.py:3-5). Proven schemes: 'work:song-x' (song_x.py:47), 'parcel:29024080530000' (parcels.py:74,82). Multi-subject events (splits/merges) are schema-supported (C1-event-layer.md:276-279).

claimant.$comment: Proven conventions: a real party, a registry routing claimant ('cook-county-tax-sale-registry', cook_parcels.py:80 — routing, not identity; recorded parties stay verbatim in the payload, C2-second-domain.md:78-80), or a named mechanical detector ('registration-conflict-check', pro_conflict.py:35).

claim.$comment: Domain payload. No floats anywhere — Decimal or int (schema.py:71-102, determinism rule C1-event-layer.md:101-102). In canonical JSON bytes a Decimal is the envelope {"__t": "decimal", "__v": "<fixed-point>"} (ri_core/serialization.py:130-131). Proven payloads: share_claims tables (pro_conflict.py:38-50); verbatim recorded parties and terms (cook_parcels.py:23-32).

ep_type.$comment: Closed set of four epistemic-provenance channel types (schema.py:55-60). Mapping onto the engine's uncertaintyType vocabulary is policy, not schema (schema.py:14-17; policy.py:65). Proven: third_party_attested for PRO registrations (pro_conflict.py:1), statutory_registry for county records (cook_parcels.py:1).

source_url.$comment: No-fabrication rule: required non-empty (schema.py:175). Real record → the resolving public URL; synthetic fixture → the format documentation it is modeled on, with the SYNTHETIC label making the distinction inspectable (C1-event-layer.md:98-100); attested retrieval → the system's public page (C2-second-domain.md:66-74).

observed_date.$comment: Canonical ISO YYYY-MM-DD, strictly validated (schema.py:105-118, :176). Drives ltime via policy.ltime_for (policy.py:103) — event time comes from the record, never from a clock (parcels.py:14-15).

prior_event_refs.$comment: Cross-event relations (may be empty; never self-referencing, schema.py:194-197). Proven use: revocation names the revoked registration (pro_conflict.py:19-20); redemption names its tax sale through the identical fold (finding F1, C2-second-domain.md:22-24).

claimValue.$comment: Mirrors _validate_claim_value (schema.py:71-102): None, bool, int, str, Decimal (envelope form), list, dict with string keys. Non-integer JSON numbers are unrepresentable here by design — floats are rejected at the schema boundary.
